title: Restricted projective modules inherit the regular algebra Tor bound
statement: Let $A,B$ be commutative rings, $\rho:A\to B$ a ring map, $E$ a projective $B$-module (maps out of $E$ lift across surjections), and $d\in\mathbf N$. If $\operatorname{Tor}^A_j(B,M)=0$ for every $A$-module $M$ and every $j>d$, with $B$ restricted along $\rho$ [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], then $\operatorname{Tor}^A_j(E,M)=0$ for every $M$ and $j>d$, with $E$ likewise restricted. The Tor functor is derived in its first argument. No finiteness condition is imposed on $E$ or $\rho$.

source.place: Tag 066H, lemma-tor-amplitude-finite-complex; Tags 066K, lemma-tor-amplitude-change-rings, and 0655. Sources checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/066H and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/066K.

proof.text: The free B-module on the underlying set of E surjects onto E by sending the basis vector indexed by x to x. Projectivity supplies a splitting. Scalar restriction retains the splitting, and the restricted free module is the direct sum of copies of restricted B, even for an infinite basis.

source.place: Tag 066H, lemma-tor-amplitude-finite-complex; Tags 066K, lemma-tor-amplitude-change-rings, and 0655. Sources checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/066H and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/066K.

proof.text: Use the natural symmetry of Tor to resolve the test module M. Tensoring its projective resolution with a direct sum of copies of restricted B commutes with that direct sum. Direct sums of modules are exact, so homology commutes with them. The Tor of the restricted free module is therefore a direct sum of the assumed zero Tor groups of B in degrees j>d. Transport this vanishing through the symmetry isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 066H, lemma-tor-amplitude-finite-complex; Tags 066K, lemma-tor-amplitude-change-rings, and 0655. Sources checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/066H and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/066K.

proof.text: Apply the fixed-second-argument left-derived tensor functor to the restricted split maps. Their composite is the identity by functoriality, so Tor of E is a retract of Tor of the restricted free module. A retract of a zero object is zero.

theorem projective_restriction_tor_bound
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (ρ : A →+* B)
    (E : ModuleCat.{u} B) (hE : Projective E) (d : ℕ)
    (hTor : ∀ M : ModuleCat.{u} A, ∀ j : ℕ, d < j →
      IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} A) j).obj
        ((restrictScalars ρ).obj (of B B))).obj M)) :
    ∀ M : ModuleCat.{u} A, ∀ j : ℕ, d < j →
      IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} A) j).obj ((restrictScalars ρ).obj E)).obj M)
